checks: Re-derived the S-nucleus peak T_b independently from the Xb4b spw25 pbcor cube (beam 0.246x0.232"): 7-channel-mean peak pixel (461,430) gives T_b(RJ)=2.89 K at 265.1 GHz, single-channel peak 3.2 K (noise-biased, 10.5 mJy/beam). Worker's 2.81 K (3-channel boxcar, 4.4 km/s channels) agrees within ~3%. Planck-equivalent 7.4 K for 2.75 K checked analytically (h nu/k=12.7 K, J(2.73)=0.12). Agree.

Continuum: native-pixel peak of the Xb4b 4-spw cont map is 1.85 mJy/beam (T_b 0.59 K) vs the worker's 1.64-1.70 mJy/beam (0.53 K) taken from the 3-px-smoothed map (s151 peak_sm). ~10% low; the dust-only Sigma and the continuum-to-line ratio should use the native peak (or state it is smoothed). Minor.

Imaging-consistency check (team/checks/q6_rev.py): smoothed Xb4b HCO+ 3-2 channels to the Xb4d beam (flux-conserving) and compared with Xb4d at S: peak per-beam values agree to 0-5% for channels 135-142 (e.g. 0.0458 vs 0.0458, 0.0460 vs 0.0471 Jy/beam); on the red side Xb4d is 10-30% higher (ch 143-147), i.e. extended red-shifted emission filtered by Xb4b, consistent with the worker's missing-flux section (0.8-0.9 at r<2-4"). Agree with the flux-recovery numbers.

By the same comparison the S-nucleus peak T_b falls from ~2.9 K (0.25") to ~1 K at the 1" Xb4d beam (peak 0.046 Jy/beam over a 12x larger beam area), a factor ~3 dilution between 0.25" and 1". The worker's report only quotes the Gaussian-source dilution 1.2-1.35 and 'filling ~0.8 for a smooth ~100 pc disk'. The empirical scale dependence (the core+pedestal structure) is not carried into the filling discussion; it is the one direct handle on filling vs excitation that the data give. Disagree that the filling discussion is complete.

Read the size/width code (s151): sizes are half-max-area diameters of a 3-px smoothed moment-0 within r<1.2-1.5" and beam-deconvolved as sqrt(D^2-bmaj*bmin); noise errors via beam-correlated injection; injection test shows +-0.03" bias for D>=0.15". Method is standard and honestly caveated (box dependence, pedestal, S/N<10 flagged tentative). Velocity-gradient smearing (G=160/44 km/s/" -> sigma 16/4 km/s) is computed correctly in order of magnitude; nuclear widths are not beam-smeared. Agree.

Virial-style masses use 1040 sigma^2 R with R = half-max radius and sigma from a single-Gaussian FWHM of non-Gaussian (W20/FWHM up to 2) profiles; presented as upper limits - acceptable, but the R convention differs from Rosolowsky & Leroy (R=1.91 sigma_r) and from the CO catalogue (deconvolved, extrapolated), so the 'matches Brunetti median' statement is only a factor-~2 comparison.

fixes.what: Turn the 0.25"->1"->(4") brightness comparison into a measured T_b(scale) / dilution relation for HCO+ and HCN 3-2 at N, S, Bridge, E1, E2: smooth the Xb4b cubes (per channel, proper elliptical kernel to the Xb4d beam, flux-conserving) and compare peak-channel (and boxcar) T_b with the native Xb4d values; also give T_b in matched 0.25" aperture-averaged form.
fixes.why: Currently filling is argued from a single Gaussian-dilution factor (1.2-1.35) plus a sub-thermal RADEX bound, yet the real peak T_b drops ~3x from 0.25" to 1" at S (my check). That pedestal/clumpiness directly measures how the filling changes with scale, tests Brunetti+2021's 'smooth medium, no trend of T_b with scale' for the dense gas, and bounds sub-beam filling (if T_b keeps rising to the finest scale, f<1 at 50 pc). Without it the 'dilution is only 1.2-1.35' sentence is misleading.
fixes.how_experts_do_it: Measure T_b at fixed physical scales (55, 120, 250 pc) by convolving to common beams (PHANGS-style) and plot T_b vs scale per region; fit a power law or a core+envelope model with beam-convolved profiles, report the implied core filling at 50 pc.

fixes.what: Make the size result robust to the core+pedestal structure: fit azimuthally averaged radial profiles / curve of growth of the moment-0 (centre at the peak, after subtracting the pedestal as a constant or second Gaussian with a fixed ~1.5-2" width taken from the Xb4d image) with a model convolved with the actual beam, and report core FWHM from that next to the half-max-area number.
fixes.why: The 2-Gaussian fit was abandoned as unconstrained; half-max area of a core on a ~30-60% pedestal is level-dependent (the half-max contour moves with the pedestal), so 0.50" at S and 0.52" at N may be biased by the pedestal. A fixed-pedestal-width fit is well constrained and would also give the core/pedestal flux split used in the summary (16-31% r<0.5").
fixes.how_experts_do_it: Fit beam-convolved 2D Gaussian+Gaussian(fixed larger width from lower-resolution data) or Sersic/exponential profiles on the image plane, using the beam PA and per-pixel correlated noise; quote FWHM with the pedestal marginalised.

fixes.what: Use the native (unsmoothed) continuum peak for T_b and dust Sigma (1.85 mJy/beam S) and say explicitly which smoothing was used where; also cross-check the sizes with the Xb4b manual 26.6 MHz cube (0.22" beam, spw25 only) or the mfs images, as the worker already proposed.
fixes.why: The 10% smoothing bias propagates to the continuum T_b, Sigma, and the line/continuum ratio; the manual cube is an independent imaging of the same data and the cheap test of imaging-dependent size systematics (beam 0.22 vs 0.25").
fixes.how_experts_do_it: Quote peak of the native pixel map with the rms, and test the key sizes on two independent imagings; flag any difference >0.05" as systematic.

fixes.what: State the virial-mass radius convention (R=1.91 sigma_r vs half-max radius) and recompute the mass with a Gaussian-equivalent sigma from the second moment (sigma_mom2 is already in s151) and with the distance 35 Mpc alternative; keep these as upper limits.
fixes.why: The comparison with the CO catalogue (virial mass 5.4e7, alpha_vir 4.3) is used to claim the clumps are CO-like; the factor-2 systematics of R and non-Gaussian sigma are of the same size as the claimed agreement.
fixes.how_experts_do_it: Rosolowsky & Leroy 2006: M_vir=1040 sigma^2 R with R=1.91 sigma_maj,deconvolved and extrapolated to zero intensity, sigma from the deconvolved moment-2 of the cube.

notes_for_questioner: (1) Does the HCO+ (and HCN) 3-2 peak T_b scale as ~constant, or fall steeply, from 55 to 250 pc? (the data suggest ~3x from 0.25" to 1" at S) - compare to the smooth CO medium of Brunetti+2021. (2) With Xb4d at 1" and the Band 7 4-3 / Band 5 2-1 at 4-9" smoothed to a common beam, can the 3-2 excitation be separated from filling at ~1-4" for N and S, as a prior for the 0.25" core? (3) The off-nuclear HCO+ clumps (sigma 23-28 km/s, 120-135 pc) are CO-like, the nuclei are 2-3x broader with strong velocity gradients (160 km/s/" at N): a Q on whether the N nuclear-disk rotation curve is resolvable in Xb4b (position-velocity cut) and what dynamical mass it implies vs Sakamoto+2014 (S: ~2e9 Msun within 200 pc).
